arm: P1_guth_gold_1938 (Guth & Gold 1938 Phys. Rev. 53:322, 5-param bounded least_squares, identical to parent receipts)
claim_scope: Statistical-methodology audit only, restricted to the Purformance HTE 2K-PUR lacquer scratch-hardness leak-free 58-observation, G=3-cluster benchmark. Does not modify or delete split-integrity-dedup-v1 or guth-gold-nested-refit-bootstrap-v1. Grants no batch-release, qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority. n=58 leak-free observations from a single formulator and a single instrument; G=3 DoE iterations is the entire population of clusters available, so no attack can supply more independent cluster-level replication than this dataset physically contains.
honest_interpretation: COVERAGE-CALIBRATION ATTACK on the module's currently-surviving significance claim 'guth_gold_directional_concordance_exceeds_chance_leak_free' (split-integrity-dedup-v1 C=0.7111 CI[0.6155,0.7980]; guth-gold-nested-refit-bootstrap-v1 CI[0.6352,0.7270], SURVIVED 2026-08-02). Both surviving CIs are built over a G=3-cluster leave-one-iteration-out structure (fold sizes 17/26/15) and never resample which points are assigned to which of the 3 DoE iterations -- that axis is structurally fixed because only 3 iterations exist in the whole population. Cameron, Gelbach & Miller 2008 (cited by the parent receipt as the bootstrap's own justification) explicitly warn that cluster-bootstrap inference is unreliable for G below roughly 20-30. This receipt MEASURES that warning directly: 1000 (protocol A, parent test-only) and 80 (protocol B, nested train-refit) independent true-null simulations (y permuted across all 58 rows, exact real X and exact real fold structure preserved, so H0: no true feature-target relationship holds exactly) were each run through the identical CI-construction machinery as the two standing receipts. PRE-REGISTERED REFUTATION CRITERION: one-sided empirical false-positive rate (fraction of null CIs whose 95% lower bound spuriously exceeds 0.5) > 7.5% (3x the nominal ~2.5%) for EITHER protocol. OBSERVED: protocol A (parent test-only, M=1000, B=2000) empirical FPR = 0.0330 (3.30%) [lower-bound-exceeds-chance], 0.0480 (4.80%) [upper-bound-below-chance], 0.0810 (8.10%) [either tail]. Protocol B (nested train-refit, M=80, B=400) empirical FPR = 0.0375 (3.75%) [lower-bound-exceeds-chance], 0.0375 (3.75%) [upper-bound-below-chance], 0.0750 (7.50%) [either tail]. VERDICT: CLAIM SURVIVES -- both protocols' empirical false-positive rates stay within the pre-registered tolerance despite G=3, so the real-data CI exclusion of 0.5 is not explained by miscalibration of the interval-construction method alone. This does not certify the standing point estimate C_obs=0.7111 is itself correct or generalizable -- only that this specific class of attack (CI miscalibration under few clusters) does/does not explain it.
protocol: leave-one-iteration-out over the 58 leak-free unique (feature,target) observations, folds 17/26/15 (identical construction as split-integrity-dedup-v1)

protocol_a_parent_test_only.description: identical bootstrap machinery as split-integrity-dedup-v1: per-fold Guth-Gold fit ONCE on true (permuted-null) training data, then B_A within-fold-stratified resamples of held-out points (no refit) recompute concordance

protocol_b_nested_train_refit.description: identical bootstrap machinery as guth-gold-nested-refit-bootstrap-v1: per-replicate per-fold resample of TRAINING rows with replacement, Guth-Gold refit from scratch on resampled (permuted-null) training data, scored against original held-out fold

refutation_criterion: one-sided empirical false-positive rate (fraction of true-null Monte-Carlo simulations, exact real X and fold structure preserved, y permuted) whose 95%% CI lower bound spuriously exceeds 0.5 chance, > 7.5%% (3x nominal ~2.5%%) for EITHER the parent test-only or the nested train-refit bootstrap protocol
